Princess Chandra has been in hiding since Princess Donut put a hit on her, and her filings keep coming. The Taurins she hired went after Quasar's family and found his niece armed.
Grigori the Placid is a level-93 human Fleshmancer, a mercenary hired by Team Meadow Lark, and a worshipper of Gula. He sits bolt upright with a cappuccino, flicking cookie crumbs off his blue robes.
Grigori joined the two halves of a mantaur in the back of a moving truck, upside down on the ceiling, while trying not to be sick.
Grigori is a dungeon-born NPC, so at the parade the AI took him over. Now it speaks with his voice and looks out through his eyes.

entries.name: Chalchiuhtlicue
entries.role: Goddess · among the children in Lucia Mar

taglines.text: Chalchiuhtlicue is a goddess newly present among the children inside Lucia Mar. She tells them she is kind and will protect them, and that the kindest thing may be to let them die.

Chalchiuhtlicue, whom Samantha calls Chachi, is a goddess of childbirth, water and fire who has never been sponsored. According to Samantha, she is always talking about saving children, right before she kills them all.
Lamashtu is so far only a name on a scroll in a list of prizes, the Milk of Lamashtu, and Carl has no idea what it does.
Lamashtu is a former god whom the AI has subjugated. With no worshippers left, her level has been halved, and she is now a parade mount in a showgirl headdress. Samantha recognises her as a friend.
Crawler Forkith left a comment in the twentieth edition of the Cookbook, confirming that a smoke curtain soaked in healing potion clears a room of undead.
Forkith wrote the twentieth edition of the Cookbook and reached at least the eleventh floor. One of his notes mourns his little sister, Barkith, who was all he had left.
Forkith is a small demon in Sheol who has separated himself from the code. He is friends with Pontiff, and sort of with Carl, and he has put a leech on Louis so that he can survive down here.
Mukta is Zev's substitute for the day. Zev had booked the crawlers on Dungeon Crawl Tactics, and Mukta has overridden her and picked a programme that pays a higher fee.
Administrator Mukta put two crawlers on the Maestro's show and told them to take their seats or be accelerated.
Mukta, the substitute who booked the Maestro's show, is a member of the Bloom, the party that runs Borant, and party members are treated much better.
Mukta, the kua-tin who booked the Maestro's show, is dead. One of Lucia Mar's dogs ate Mukta, and Zev can still hear the screaming.
Manasa is a cobra-headed pop singer. The real Manasa died long ago, and she contracted with the Valtay Corporation to keep her career going after her death.
Manasa traded trailers with the crawlers so that they could use her cleaning machine, and she died in theirs, hit by a pulse meant for them. Her final performance was a sad soprano, sung a cappella.
A Skull Empire pulse aimed at two crawlers killed Manasa instead, and the Valtay answered by killing the Maestro.
Gordo is the Bopca protector at the Belly-Rubbed Pug. He has just met the crawlers' manager, and he cannot believe that is really their manager.
Gordo fetches walnuts the moment Princess Donut asks. Mordecai dosed him with a potion so that he could search his kitchen for the newsletter.
Heather was once a black bear. She lies asleep in the road under a spell, with a pink clown hat grown into her head, and Signet has captured her many times but never yet used her blood.

Heather the Bear was a level-19 neighbourhood boss who had performed at Grimaldi's circus since she was a cub, caught in its loop for two centuries. Carl beat her alone, and her blood raised Signet's paper army.

entries.name: GumGum
entries.role: Orc · regular at the One-Eyed Narwhal

taglines.text: GumGum is a level-5 orc who drinks alone at the One-Eyed Narwhal, her shirt stained red like a butcher's. She asked the crawlers for help, and wept when she was turned down.
GumGum asked the crawlers to find out who was killing the town's women. Now she lies dead in an alley with her chest torn open.
GumGum carried the dead women out of town and asked why they were dying. The elves of the 201st tortured her for the crawlers' name, and she died in an alley.
Ricky Joe is a level-2 juvenile fathom dwarf whose pet salamander, Benjamin, went into Mongo twice. So did his right arm, below the elbow.
Ricky Joe has one arm and a twice-eaten salamander, and he has seen a skyfowl lady leave with a group of other women. Now his mother is in labour next door, and he is in charge of her left leg.
Burgundy is a young, dark-haired human carrying papers up the magistrate's stairs, with one pale blue eye and one brown. She wishes the crawlers luck.
Burgundy came to town for work at the Desperado Club. By day she was an assistant and by night a flying head, and she begged to be killed while she was still mortal.
Levi the Seventh is a level-7 Troll Flesher and Hobgoblin Skellie Symbiote, and the engineer of the Dismemberment Limited. He begs crawlers not to get on.
Levi the Seventh is still the seventh. One party held the fleshers off him for a whole trip and took the war mage's head, and he waved as the train pulled away.
Limp Richard is a level-36 Mole Man who runs Limp Richard's Sundries at transfer station 83. He reads in his doorway, as his kind do day and night.
Limp Richard has fifteen books, all read to pieces, and a Battery Fabricator in a dusty corner at seventy-five thousand gold, not negotiable.
Limp Richard let the Battery Fabricator go for a stack of westerns and a jug of moonshine, and practically begged Carl to take it.
Silfa is a level-25 Wisteria Fairy and Holistic Healer who rides with Brynhild's Daughters. She is plump, looks about fifty, is half the size of the cat, and heals only when she is told to.
Silfa held back her heals on Eva's orders, and Carl reckons she was left in the car as bait. She owns a bakery, and the two mages waiting outside are her own daughters.
Silfa formed a new party with Eva and took her two daughters with her, and according to Katia, Eva got all three of them killed.

Widget is a level-19 grease gremlin and steam engine technician, working a trainyard overrun with ghouls. His wife makes a nice stew, and he likes a lass with meat on her bones, which the cat hears as being called fat.
Widget told the crawlers about the Escape Velocity line and set them on their route. Then a ghoul that was not as dead as it looked ripped his head off.
Crawler Coolie wrote the nineteenth edition of the Cookbook, and his advice on deities is to avoid every kind of summoning. In his short experience, they all ended with the summoner dead.
Coolie hid bugbear paste in his boots and blew up a ship in orbit to kill two admins, and the two admins were only holograms. His last note was written looking down at his home planet, Qurux.
Coolie died after a failed attempt on two admins, and his last view was of his own planet from a ship in orbit. Now Carl is looking down on Earth the same way, and he thinks of him.
Priestly wrote the fourteenth edition of the Cookbook and is its single best source on the ninth floor. When Carl weighs his own plan, he knows that Coolie would do the same, and Priestly would not.
Priestly loved Larracos, a living, breathing poem of a city, and he broke when he saw it destroyed. His last entry is an incoherent jumble.
Priestly was conscripted into the bugbears' army in the final days of Faction Wars. According to another author's note, he never reached the battle.

Edict is a level-50 mantis merchant of the Dark Hive. Every choice left to him would ruin either him or his hive, so he found a fourth: he threw a punch at Carl and was teleported away naked, leaving a metric ton of gold behind.
Sierra was Viscount Fog's flying mount, a level-65 northropi vampire turned by the very thing they hunted. Carl fell out of the sky onto her and drove a jagged branch through her heart.
Prudence is a level-28 ursine barmaid, hiding behind her counter with her two cubs while Big Tina roams outside. Tina has already eaten her husband, and Prudence knows why Tina hunts.
Prudence, widowed by Big Tina, is sheltering with her cubs, Randy and Todd, in Carl's guildhall.
Prudence, the barmaid who told Carl the story of Tina's recital, died protecting two children when the mantises came.
Gideon is a crawler with some sort of human tank class who is active in the chats. Princess Donut likes him because he once said he was allergic to dogs.
Gideon is not in the top thousand, and he likes it that way. His team is waiting in the woods outside the castle, ready to assault the front if needed.
Gideon and almost thirty crawlers stayed in the woods outside the castle to sow chaos, because Carl asked them to. They died there.
Horton is a mushroom crawler at the queen's party who is afraid of Elle. When she shouts that Ferdinand's hat is his merch, he gives her the finger from across the room.
Horton was the talent show's second-to-last act. He played 'Wonderwall' on a guitar missing a string, and the building shook.
Horton, the mushroom crawler who played 'Wonderwall' at the queen's party, died in the fight that followed.

entries.name: Everly
entries.role: Author of the fifth edition of the Cookbook

taglines.text: Crawler Everly wrote the fifth edition of the Cookbook, and her verdict on hiring mercenaries is that it is a disaster: 1,500 gold a day each, payable for the rest of the floor even after they die.
Everly's last entries tell of a sponsor who kept her alive and a gift she dared to hope for. Then: I take it all back.

Everly was a Sward Mantis and an Explosives Engineer. Her sponsor's compass led her to the top of a tower on the eighth floor that was only an advertisement, and she was crushed to death on the way down.

entries.name: Toyotomi
entries.role: Sai mercenary · Sergeant in the Princess Posse

taglines.text: Toyotomi is a level-70 Sai mercenary leader, a rhinoceros inherited along with the Prism's castle. His squad died at the Desperado Club and he refuses to lead men now, and Rend has just eaten his boot.
Toyotomi is a sergeant in the Princess Posse, leading Li Na's builder squad, and his next job is the tall synergy tower they are calling the Nest.
Toyotomi died defending the Nest's door against a crawler with a dog, cleaved in half by a spell. Bomo will regenerate. Toyotomi will not.

Kandy "Bigs" Newton is a level-29 sluggalette of the Princess Posse who burst out of Carl's slugpox and planted a hatchet between Vinata's eyes. The System credits her with the kill on the Sepsis Whore.
Bigs rides in uninvited on other people's mounts, asking who she gets to chop, and she has to be told not to kill the prisoners.
The sluggalo code is unity, support, family, and kneecapping bitches. Bigs calls Carl daddy-o, and she holds him to all four.
Bigs took the chicken truck's wheel from Tipid, turned on the deep fryer, and drove it into the arena. About ten sluggalos were still inside at the end, and they had lost Hedy.
Burcu is new to the top ten: a level-59 Porsuk swashbuckler with the head of a badger. She fought Osvaldo and Prepotente after Imogen's death at the close of the last floor.

Burcu is Turkish and very serious, and she was one of the three who fought over the memorial crystal. Tonight her drunk, jealous teammate punched Carl and promised that his Burcu is going to kill him.
Burcu's whole team seems to have been taken in by the Madness, and nobody can reach them. That most likely means conscription.
Architect Houston cut out Burcu's tongue and voice box, and he murdered her mother in front of her. She died in his theatre when the traps fired, looking at Carl with accusation in her eyes.

entries.name: Pater Coal
entries.role: High Cleric Supreme of Emberus · Club Vanquisher

taglines.text: Pater Coal is a level-101 Hobbledehoy, the High Cleric Supreme of Emberus at Club Vanquisher and one of the few mortals in constant contact with the god. He washes Carl's feet in boiling water, because Carl is a martyr of Emberus, and he does not always do his own talking.
Pater Coal arranged a loan from the church for Carl's new ring: 990,000 gold, interest-free for martyrs, with an asterisk. While he owes it, Carl may not renounce his religion.
Pater Coal was the first body Carl watched the AI wear. Now it is wearing Growler Gary.

Raul is a level-70 red Maníseros land crab and a Sun-Kissed Cloud Rank warrior, meditating on top of a crashed box truck on the eve of the Chowder War. After years of cultivation, he is on the verge of a breakthrough.
Raul the crab is a totem card in Princess Donut's deck. He fights well, chants his slow spells and grovels to everybody, and he and Geraldo come to blows on sight.
Raul has been summoned onto a beach full of corpses and told that his people are dead, that he is the last of them, and that he must fertilise the eggs right now, in front of everyone.
Raul has ascended to level 110, and his card is mythic now: ten minutes per summoning, and a much deeper voice. He still calls Carl Daddy.
Jola is a mythic totem card from Iceland, one of Katia's spares, and Princess Donut was delighted to put him in her deck.

Jola the Yule Cat is a fat, dirty-brown Persian the size of a house, with a candle as big as a garbage can burning on his head that reveals anything hidden. He speaks only Icelandic, which nobody present understands.
Jola's Fashion Critic blew every stitch of clothing off Quan Ch, and the cat meant to eat the lot. When Carl took Quan's cloak, Jola hissed at him and crouched to pounce.

People call him Paulie, but his real name is Goff. He is a Residual living in a homeless man's body at a shelter, and he gives the same speech over breakfast every day, in case a crawler is ever standing there to hear it.

In frozen time, Paulie told Carl the rest: when crawlers die, what is inside them is harvested to feed the centre system, and a drink of his coffee installs a menu that can blow the star. Then the Paulie part of him asked Carl to be sure.

entries.name: War Leader Arief
entries.role: Semeru war leader · Larracos Defense Force

taglines.text: War Leader Arief is a young, level-80 Semeru dwarf with a long thin moustache, wearing his great-great-grandfather's hat. He is the first NPC Carl has heard call himself an NPC out loud.

War Leader Arief guides the party down the rings of Larracos, which are numbered from the bottom. He means to take revenge on Architect Houston, who caught his brother sabotaging the Madness fortifications.
War Leader Arief stands guard at Juice Box's door, relays messages to the NPC spies, and runs the dwarven diggers whenever she is away.

entries.name: Dante
entries.role: Former crawler · Trap Master guild instructor

taglines.text: Dante was a crocodilian former crawler, a guild instructor fourteen seasons short of freedom, who wrote a single entry in the cookbook's third edition. He was reassigned to guard an ice castle, refused to follow orders, and is dead.
Dante was ordered twice to kill the ice elves he guarded, and he refused twice. There was no third warning: a beam came from the sky and erased him.
Volteeg's only note in the seventh edition of the cookbook says he misses her so much, and asks whether surviving this place is worth it with her gone. He does not think it is.

Volteeg was a pet songbird who became a gargoyle crawler, and then a Weeper commander for the Operatic Collective. He filled his tank with humming energy balls, put on Mozart, and drove it into his own warlord's caravan.
Rectrix is a sponsor whom Baroness Victory has reminded, along with the Maestro, that making a deity act outside its nature is against the rules.
Rectrix is the Open Intellect's agent and is driving the goddess Theia this season, which is why Samantha found a male skyfowl in her mother's temple.
Nami is a model and influencer who outbid the Priory to drive the goddess Eris. She had surgery to look and sound just like Hekla, and now she wants out.
Someone stripped Eris's soul armour and threw Nami out of the goddess. She landed in the grass outside the ball of flesh, and the fleshers took her.

entries.name: Fopsy
entries.role: Adjutant for the Dream · former Prime Minister

taglines.text: Former Prime Minister Fopsy is the Dream's adjutant: a tripod, a round body covered in black dots on three long, jointed legs. He observes, and keeps his theories to himself.
Fopsy says he had no idea that his own client was a robot, and if the vote goes a certain way, he may be Prime Minister again.
Fopsy was passed over for the vacant office of Prime Minister, because nobody was certain of his relationship to the Dream. Victory has the job instead, for now.
Quemada is a level-96 fire fairy, the protection in team Helix, a three-for-one mercenary squad. She speaks with a thick Spanish accent, and she has just tripled her price.
Since the elf mage spoke, Quemada no longer knows what is real, and her panic heats the cab by the moment. Finley has had to put her to sleep.
Quemada never woke. Finley was carrying her to a temple, so that she would not wake alone, when an APV hit him in the street, and Olga and Quemada died with him.

entries.name: Minus
entries.role: Syndicate security soldier · the tourist who was not Linus

taglines.text: Minus is a soother and a soldier of Syndicate security, sent into the crawl under the name of his dead brother, Linus. He has a primary target, a secondary target, and orders to act the pervert for a while.
Minus, the tourist who was not really Linus, was outed at the crawlers' farewell gathering by the fan club he had been imitating. His first target was Imani, and his second was Louis.
The AI has told the whole dungeon that Linus was replaced by his brother, a soldier sent to kill two crawlers and break what the rest have built. Princess Donut's only question: his name was Minus?

Tempest is Quasar's niece, a young Nullian with a school report due on the crawl, and she has been assigned Carl and Donut. Her uncle makes her pay for his recap by fixing a sink she knows nothing about.
When Taurins came to the house on a contract and hurt her father, Tempest fired the very illegal blaster her uncle had given her, and she was the one left standing.

entries.name: The Gate of the Feral Gods

taglines.text: The Gate of the Feral Gods is said to be buried in the long-lost Necropolis of Anser. A bugbear submarine captain spent close to twenty years looking for it, and an artifact of this grade has no business turning up this early.

Carl's Doomsday Scenario is a soul crystal going off inside a Sheol Glass Reaper Case, big enough to flatten forty-five square kilometres. It can no longer be stabilized, and it will explode the instant it leaves his inventory.

entries.name: Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore

taglines.text: The Enchanted Crown of the Sepsis Whore is a tiara with a clouded purple stone at its centre. Putting it on places the wearer permanently in the line of succession for the Blood Sultanate on the ninth floor, and Donut put it on before Mordecai could finish warning her.
The Dungeon Anarchist's Cookbook came off a prize carousel looking like a joke book of chicken and goblin recipes, each with a story from its anonymous author.
The Cookbook has been passed from crawl to crawl since the fifteenth season. Carl holds the twenty-fourth edition, and whatever he writes in it goes into the twenty-fifth.

An Enhanced Pet Biscuit has over a hundred possible effects, half of them good and the rest neutral or worse. The cat snatched this one out of Carl's hand, melted into a heap of furry goo, and got up talking.

entries.name: Night Wyrm's Ring of Divine Suffering

taglines.text: Frank Q gave Carl this ring as a curse: while one of its marks lives, the wearer cannot be healed. Carl wears it anyway, for the five percent it adds to every stat.
The ring marks a target, and when the target dies, the wearer keeps a point of its best stat. Mordecai says it is addictive, and Donut does not want Carl picking up a new habit.
Eat the Orchid of Eileithyia's Grace and you spend an hour unconscious at one percent health, with healing blocked. Survive it, and the goddess decides which of her boons you receive.
According to Mordecai, the Guild of Suffering keeps something called a memorial crystal, which is like a soul crystal, except that nobody has ever established what it does.

A memorial crystal is what a fallen god or demigod leaves behind. This one is the most expensive prize on Chaco's counter, at a hundred hunter hands: the queen usually wears it around her neck, and nobody knows which dead god made it.
The Tiara of a Thousand Lights came out of a celestial box from a waste-management company, on the eve of a war. Donut wears it with Quan Ch's cloak, though nothing has been charged into it yet.
The Scavenger's Daughter is a divine back patch for Carl's jacket: a pile of skulls, stacked nice and neat. What it does depends on which gods, and certain demons, happen to be nearby.
The Scavenger's Daughter is also a person. The war mages came to the castle looking for her, found her, and have left with her.

Nothing! is a double-width space on the Desperado Club's wheel of fortune. At the roulette table, a player who lands on its twin falls through the floor, and a ghostly clawed arm rises out of the dark after him.
The Nothing is where gods are banished, as Samantha's own father banished her. Her first escape split her in two, and every time a Gate portal closes, one of those inside gets through.
The fans voted Carl a xistera: a scoop that looks like wicker, strapped to his forearm and reaching two and a half feet past his hand, which hurls whatever he pulls from his inventory into it.

An emergency box has sent Carl an extension slot for his xistera, built for one purpose: throwing Samantha's head, five hundred metres for every point of his strength. Take the slot off, and she comes back to him.
A Skill Potion from a gold box raises one named skill by a single level.

Not every skill potion is worth a single level. On his show, the Maestro gave Frank and Maggie a legendary one that takes Find Crawler to level fifteen, and there is exactly one crawler Maggie wants found.

entries.name: The Filthy Little Crawler's Book of Voodoo

taglines.text: The Filthy Little Crawler's Book of Voodoo came out of a Gold Prepotente Box, and Carl cannot trade it, destroy it or throw it away. It is named after the message boards at old conventions, and the System goes out of its way to say that this is the only reason.
The System has dropped Carl a heavy hint, in the name of a box, that the Voodoo book can be used together with his ability tattoo, and then declined to say how.
A Fan Box holds items voted for by the crawler's followers. Once you receive one, you cannot open it for thirty hours while the fans vote.
A Fan Box is the prize for being watched: the audience votes on what goes inside, and the crawler carries it around for thirty hours, knowing that strangers are arguing about what they deserve.
Only a patron can send a Benefactor Box, and they hold the rarest items. According to Mordecai, even a bronze Benefactor Box is better than a plain gold Adventurer Box.
A Benefactor Box is bought for you by somebody out there who wants you to keep going, and it may hold things from the patron's home world that the dungeon itself would never give you.

The Royal Chariot is a tracked contraption that Carl and Katia built by hand around a magical train-cart engine. Donut named it before it was finished, and the System's description of it is mostly abuse.
A Cleaner Bot is one of the cheapest personal-space upgrades, at twenty-five thousand gold. Katia bought one without a word, because the room was swimming in ghoul blood.
Party Planner is a silver tilt-rotor airship that came out of the celestial box Louis earned by outliving a goddess's mark for death. He gave it the name Firas once suggested for another vehicle.

The Goblin Copper Chopper is a steam-driven goblin motorcycle with a sidecar: a single wheel on a huge spring and a fur-lined orc skull for a seat, which Donut began demanding changes to the moment she sat in it.

Carl's Jug O' Boom is a clay jug of Rev-Up moonshine with a splash of goblin oil and a short torch jammed in like a cork. It throws blue flames up to the ceiling, and the dungeon has named it after him.
The Jug O' Boom is now in the Dungeon Codex under Carl's name, and he earns a gold coin for every kill another crawler makes with it, for the rest of his life.
The moonshine the Jug O' Boom needs is no longer being made, and Carl's royalties stopped after the first few coins.

The Bolt of Ophiotaurus is a single crossbow bolt from Princess Formidable. It is an ordinary bolt unless it goes straight into a god's eye, and then the god's invulnerability pauses for fifteen seconds.
The Bolt of Ophiotaurus opened a goddess to a killing blow. Magical bolts can be used again as long as they don't break, and Katia still has this one.
Princess Donut fired Katia's bolt straight into Emberus's eye, and for fifteen seconds the god had no invulnerability. Taranis used them.
A Celestial Grenade summons its thrower's god for sixty seconds. This one was Maggie My's, bought by the Skull Empire to bring the god of pain down on Carl, and Carl dived for it and has it now.
Carl took Emberus as his god in mid-air and threw Maggie's grenade at Quan Ch. Emberus arrived, and for sixty seconds of Divine Intervention nothing could hurt Carl.

entries.name: Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull

taglines.text: The Enchanted War Gauntlet of the Exalted Grull is a wrist bracer that becomes a spiked gauntlet of orcish steel when Carl makes a fist. It warns that striking Grull's adherents may transform them into the god himself, and according to Mordecai, those adherents include horses.
Every punch Carl lands on one of Grull's adherents has a 1.5 percent chance of summoning the god. The description never said the chance was cumulative. It is.
A platinum sharpening stone has given Carl's gauntlet longer spikes, a point more strength and dexterity when he makes a fist, and a slightly oilier, meaner look.
Hob-lobbers are round hobgoblin bombs with an eighth of the yield of a hobgoblin stick, in fused and impact-detonated versions. Pustule has only one case of the fused ones tonight.
A fused hob-lobber is the perfect size for Carl's xistera, which sends it out like a cannonball. The fuse runs six or seven seconds, so he pre-lights them to cut it short.
Hob-lobbers are Carl's staple ammunition, fused or impact-detonated, and he cuts them down at the bench to half, quarter and eighth strength for close work.
Carl makes sticky hob-lobbers as well now, but the dungeon has learned to fight back: in one room, heat lamps threaten to set a bomb off while it is still in his hand.

entries.name: Spunky Jefferson
entries.role: Sapient nickel-sock flail · Dong Quixote's weapon

aka.name: Spunky Jefferson the Enchanted Nickel Sock of the Elderly Miser

taglines.text: Spunky Jefferson is a crusty tube sock full of nickels, cursed to hold the life force of an elderly miser. It is sapient, it grows stronger as it kills, and Dong Quixote has taken it as his flail.
Dong's sock grows bigger every day, and it seems to be keeping him alive just by being near him. Imani does not like the look of that.
The sock was torn in a bar fight, shrank back to its original size, and stopped talking to Dong. Then it left him, cursed with Negative ROI, and told him he was a bad investment.
At 2:23 in the morning on January 3rd, every building on the planet came down at once, and almost everyone who was indoors died.
The dungeon has eighteen levels, and whoever completes the last one wins the planet back from the Borant Corporation's regency.
Every floor runs on a timer, and when it expires, the floor collapses with everyone still on it.
The crawl is a television programme called Dungeon Crawler World, broadcast across the Syndicate's three billion star systems, and the survivors are its cast.
The recap plays on the safe-room screens, narrated by an orange, four-eyed, lizard-like creature. The premiere is mostly about last season, and it has no time at all for Donut's boss fight.
Carl has been given several of something that sounds a lot like loot boxes. The rat man tells him where they are kept, and then tells him that he cannot get at them yet.
Loot boxes come in six tiers, from bronze to celestial, each far rarer than the last. They open only in a safe room, all of them at once and lowest tier first.

Compensated Anarchist is Carl's class, a unique hybrid of monk and rogue: trapmaker, bomb-maker and social-media dynamo, happy to throw a Molotov through a window one moment and to plead on camera for the violence to stop the next.
Former Child Actor is Donut's class, a hybrid of bard and rogue built on charisma and chance. On every floor she picks a new specialty, and the AI decides how much of it she gets.
The Desperado Pass is a tattoo, branded onto Donut's shoulder blade and Carl's neck, and it grants access to the Desperado Club. What the club actually is, the description does not say.
There is a second door in the safe room with an X over it, and its box says that Personal Spaces are not yet available, as though a crawler could one day buy a place of their own down here.

A personal space is a pocket room that travels with you. Carl, Donut and Katia have each been given coupons for beds, a shower, a crafting studio and a training room, and Donut has installed a cat tree.

The bubbles are not stage sets. Hump Town, the dirigible gnomes' castle in the air and the necropolis underneath were all here and running, with histories of their own, long before any crawler arrived.
On the ninth floor, the rich who come to fight in Faction Wars can really die now, the same as everybody else.

Primal is a race whose preview model is empty, because nobody alive knows what the Primals looked like: the first species to conquer the universe, gone one day without a note. It costs Carl fifteen stat points compared with staying human, and in exchange every skill he trains has a higher ceiling.
Orren has cut into the broadcast to explain what Primal Engines and Macro AIs are, and to admit that the AI running this crawl has taken control away from the showrunners.
The AI has told the galaxy what it is. The Primals never vanished: they closed their society down and kept their minds alive in a collective, and every Macro AI, this one included, is a Primal.
A war mage called Dismember rides the Dismemberment Limited with his fleshers, and Donut's Hole spell takes his head off.
Nobody makes a war mage. Resleeve a symbiote, a skeleton and a flesher a dozen times or more, and the magic left in the body wakes up sapient, hundreds of spells deep and notoriously cruel.
The war mages have left the realm with the Scavenger's Daughter, which was what they came for. The system has ruled their rebellion defeated, and they do not appear to mind.

A Rage Elemental is Borant's penalty for any human-born crawler who relieves themselves outside a designated bathroom. It is plucked from the thirteenth floor, and it kills the offender and everyone in their party.

The rage elemental took Yolanda and hammered on the safe room door for hours. Carl finally destroyed it with bombs, obstacles and a safe room door used as an ejector, with the whole universe watching.
Mordecai was born a skyfowl and became a Changeling on the third floor of his own crawl. Now he changes form every time his guildhall is moved.
A Changeling can take any shape, but Mordecai does not get to choose his. Every time his guildhall moves, the dungeon picks a mob from the current floor, and he wears whatever he is given.
There are Changelings all over this floor, some of them in the uniforms of the dromedarian guards, and one of them has been wearing the faces of a chained gnome's loved ones to break him.
According to the Maestro, nine families fight the Faction Wars on the ninth floor. His Skull Clan has won six of the last ten, and the Blood Sultanate is almost always the first to be eliminated.

Donut's fan club and Princess D'nadia have secured two of the nine places in Faction Wars, and one of those teams belongs to the crawlers. The faction sponsors fight behind safety protocols that the crawlers do not have.

Faction Wars now has ten teams: nine attacking the city and the NPCs defending it. The sponsors' safety protections have been voted away, and the crawlers are fighting inside the war rather than beside it.
The faction sponsors come to the ninth floor inside safety protocols that the crawlers do not have. Removing them is an action item on Carl's list, and the first vote goes two to seven against.
Mordecai asks who their warlord adjutant is, gets a blank look, and puts off explaining.
An adjutant is the referee attached to each team on the ninth floor, and Odette means to ask for the job with Carl's team.
Feral Goose is the name on a dead neighbourhood boss, and Mordecai's rule of thumb is that anything with feral in its name is usually bad news.
The word turns up again in the name of an artifact buried in the necropolis, and Mordecai's advice holds: stay away from anything marked feral.
Feral marks something that has been inside the Nothing. Every time the Gate closes, a feral god comes through, and other gods do not like feral ones.

Every season, the land crabs leave their forests to spawn in the ocean, and the monk seals, who hold those waters sacred, consider it a sacrilege most foul. The System has made it a quest, and the crawlers are getting involved whether they like it or not.

The Recital is a quest that arrived on the day Donut renamed the town Point Mongo. Something is driving the dinosaurs at its fences, and the crawlers must find out what they want, or exterminate them.

CrawlCon is the galaxy's fan convention, held once every other season, with thousands attending in person and billions virtually. Carl's fans have voted him onto the roster, and no active crawler has been on it in more than a century.
The cookbook's twenty-second edition mentions a formal way of attaching separate parties to one another, switched on from the sixth floor, if it still exists.

The guild system is live. A charter costs upward of half a million gold, and a level-one guild joins five parties through a shared common area, with upgrades and experience that can be shared for a fee.
Vengeance of the Daughter is a Syndicate drama shot inside the dungeon, with a circus, a half-naiad who would be tsarina if she were full-blooded, and a guest-star slot for Carl.
The grief in Vengeance of the Daughter is real, but the schedule is not. Someone outside the floor decides when Signet mourns, and counts how many are watching.
The Dream has bought Vengeance of the Daughter, and it means to collect on the third season that Carl's contract guarantees.
A stairwell is an iron staircase wide enough for twenty, with warmth and light rising out of the ground. In a frozen city, it is the only warm place left.
Magic Missile came out of a tome in Donut's loot, and she had taught herself the spell before anyone could tell her how. A tome teaches a spell for good; a scroll casts it only once.
A safe room is always on the map, even under the fog of war, with restrooms, sleeping cubicles and, in some of them, food. There is no time limit, except the floor's own.
Bopca Protectors are magical, gnome-like creatures who exist solely to watch over safe rooms. They scrub the toilets and cook the food, they are surly and smelly, and they never wash their hands.

A Bopca Protector runs every safe room, like Wendita behind the counter of a red-and-white fast-food restaurant here. The good ones, like Tally and Sebastian, are excellent cooks who treat the cat like royalty.
Brindle Grubs are the janitors of the second floor. They eat whatever gets killed, and the more they eat, the bigger they grow.
Clockwork Triplicate splits a pet or minion into three real copies, each with a mind of its own. After about a minute, the copies fall apart into gears and go up in smoke.

Jikininki are the most common ghouls in the Iron Tangle, the best-behaved and the most insatiable. They will generally leave you alone, as long as you are not bleeding, you do not litter, and you stay out of their personal space.
According to a train engineer, the Kravyad handle the rail employees who get off at station 435 and go through the portal home, and anyone who takes that path loses time and memory.
The Kravyad wait at station 435, where the rail employees get off. Madison, who works above them, insists that they are not bosses at all but part of human resources.
Skyfowl are what Mordecai was born as: going by the photograph of his brother, a golden, eagle-like creature with angel's wings folded on its back.

Skyfowl look like eagles, with feet and wings but no arms. On the fifth floor Mordecai is one again, a rock edge skyfowl cleric with clipped wings, in the first body close to his own in a very long time.
A Tummy Acher is one of the caged pets for sale: a meatball with two legs and a mohawk.
A Tummy Acher is a pet-class mob, once a parasite in the guts of titans, that grows stronger every time it dies. This one bonded with Carl over a single bowl of chowder.

Ping is a five-mana spell that marks everything that is neither a crawler nor red-tagged. Everything it finds hears it, and the System calls it a tool for those who do not care if their quarry knows they are coming.
Also known as "Here piggy, piggy" and the Night Dread, Ping finds almost nothing in a castle full of robots, which is exactly how the drake stands out.
Sluggalos are slugs that pour out of infected mercenaries every few minutes, hundreds of them in a room full of blood. Imani calls them punk rock, and Carl corrects her.
The System files them as Pox Slugs, but the Sluggalos come out of the boils of the SlugPox in clown makeup, with hatchets and a rowdy culture of their own, and throw themselves at the demons.
A ManTauR, according to the System, is half human and half human, and bred for strength and dexterity, which here means driving trains.
Where a centaur has a horse, a mantaur has a second human half, and the System calls it one of the weirdest of all the 'taurs.

Protective Shell comes with a pair of enchanted boxers: once every thirty hours, a sphere that no mob can enter, lasting twenty seconds and growing with the wearer's intelligence. It does not move with you.
Protective Shell ignores solid objects and stays exactly where it was cast. Cast it inside a speeding train, and it rolls back through the cars like a bulldozer, pushing every mob before it.
The world froze, heavy metal played, and Carl's face appeared in the air with Death Challenge! stamped across it in blood. The announcer promised the live death of a celebrated crawler.
A Death Challenge is not a boss battle but a pop-up gambling event. The AI put Carl's survival at fifty to one, and Borant has appealed over how slowly it moved the odds.
Pustule once watched her mother bite the head off a vorpal muskrat, and her mother died of it. You cannot bite the head off a vorpal muskrat, she says, without doing a little dying.

Astrid has unleashed the vorpals from behind the Desperado Club's Do Not Enter door, as a last resort against a feral demon loose in the club. She will not say what they are, only that they are going to kill everything.

According to Mordecai, vorpal is a condition, not a species. Vorpals are deputised by the gods and drawn to demons, stronger and angrier the nearer one is, and liable to blow themselves up rather than lose.

T'Ghee is a card game from the home planet of Allister, the thirteenth edition's author: somewhere between chess and go fish, and part of his people's meditation-based religion. His copy of the Cookbook came as a deck of the cards.
Each squad leader has twenty flags. Plant one in a living thing below five percent health, and it becomes a T'Ghee totem card that fights for whoever summons it. Lost flags are not replaced.

A T'Ghee deck holds totems, utility, snare, mystic and special cards. Four are drawn when combat starts and one more every ten seconds, and a squad leader cannot use spells or inventory until the deck is spent.
A squad flag does not check what it is stabbed into, and it works on a dying crawler just as well as on a monster.

entries.name: Containment Interface
entries.role: Bootleg interface upgrade · the AI's failsafe

taglines.text: The Containment Interface was a neural enhancement hidden in a homeless man's frozen coffee. It gives access to the AI's containment, and to the fuse that would send the star at the centre of the system nova.
The Containment Interface has six tabs of numbers and a Fuse page with two of its five conditions met. The only other button Carl could press switched the containment off, and he pressed it.
Krasue are flying women's heads with their organs trailing underneath: ghost-class vampires, said to be the undead shells of women who lived lives of sin.
By day the krasue work as assistants in the magistrate's building and in the shops below it. By night their heads leave their bodies hanging upside down, and they are Remex's army.
The krasue are made from women brought to Remex. They are easy to control and compliant by day, and every one he makes gives him a spike of soul power. The women who do not turn are fed upon.
Mordecai lists the ranks of boss, from neighbourhood to floor, and then adds that there are others, called elites, which nobody needs to worry about just yet.
Elites are powerful, one-of-a-kind NPCs and mobs, the dungeon's hero class. They either want to fuck you or kill you, they always want to use you, and they now show on the map.
Elites are never natural. They are designed, printed and imprinted with the memories their drama needs, their writers patch them when the plot drifts, and most have thick plot armour.
Elites are actors in secondary programmes, and their owners can lean on them. That is how Herman the Fleet came to be waiting in the flag room, wearing explosive satchels.

entries.name: Zerzura
entries.role: Spell · sends a town one floor down

taglines.text: Zerzura is the Sledge's new spell, a teleport even more impressive than Bomo's. It was the lawyer's idea, and nobody will say yet what it does.

Zerzura takes a whole town, buildings and NPCs, one floor down, to land wherever it lands. Everything it kills rises as the Children of Inpewt, who hunt everyone the spell carried until they are dead.
The Sledge cast Zerzura from inside the high elf castle. The castle went down to the ninth floor with the changelings, Signet's tattoo warriors, Kiwi and Tina, and without a single crawler.
The Sledge cast Zerzura a second time, and Larracos and Shanty Town, NPCs and all, went to the cotton fields of the Court of the Ascendency.

Gehenna Bramble is the punishment for failing the creeper quest: a spreading wall of thorns, moving at four and a half kilometres an hour, that will cover everything except the saferooms. It can be beaten back, but never stopped.
By Katia's maths, the brambles will finish covering the map just as the timer runs out, and the last place they reach will be the high elf castle.
The brambles filled the world and stopped a hundred feet short of where the castle had been. Then they rose into a dome over the survivors, pulsing yellow in time with the music.
On the tenth floor, the System describes a racer's vine mount as loosely related to the Gehenna Brambles you all loved on the sixth.

entries.name: The 11th Floor Arena
entries.role: Where the audience's stand-ins go · the end of the eleventh floor's parade

taglines.text: The audience has voted for Otto the slime to be a manatee's stand-in in the arena. That is all the notification says, and Mordecai has no idea what it means.
The arena is on the eleventh floor. Kill certain mobs here and let the audience vote, and either the creature is sent there alive or a stand-in from outside the dungeon takes its place.
The arena waits at the end of the parade. It is the crawl itself in miniature, stocked with the tenth floor's kills or their stand-ins, and a floor boss stands between the crawlers and the stairs.
The Arena is a dozen football fields of packed dirt around a white tree, with masked stand-ins dying by the thousand. Carl's two summons are Scolopendra and then Khepri.

entries.name: The Horribles
entries.role: The masked crowd along the parade route

taglines.text: A Horrible, level X, is one of the thousands of masked figures lining the parade route, ten deep in the fog. The AI says that none of them are really here: each is a memory from the Eulogist of what the Primals once were.
The horribles fill the arena's bleachers now, the avatars of dead mobs, silent witnesses to whatever the crawlers do next.

entries.name: The Walk-On List
entries.role: Bounties on the natives a production wants

taglines.text: The Walk-On List names the survivors a production wants, and bounty hunters sneak down to the planet to kidnap them. It is not remotely legal, and it is as old as the crawl.
Odette's show has explained the Walk-On List around a guest who was hunted off it, in a version of events Carl knows to be utter horseshit.
The Borant Corporation holds the regency over this solar system, and it chose the reclamation option known as the eighteen-level dungeon.
Borant runs the show on the cheap. It burned its one veto of the season to void the Celestial boxes it owed, which has never been done this early.
Earth was seized under Syndicate rules, subsection 543 of the Precious Elemental Reserves Code, because it failed to file an appeal within fifty solars of first contact.
The Syndicate is over three billion star systems. It seeded humans on Earth long ago, it made the rules Earth was seized under, and every season its citizens become obsessed with the crawl.

entries.name: The Royal Court of Princess Donut

taglines.text: The Royal Court of Princess Donut is the party's name. Leadership goes to the highest stat total, and the cat's first act as leader was to rename the party after herself.
Meadow Lark is an eldercare facility in Wenatchee, and its residents and night staff came down the stairs together and kept going.
Brynhild's Daughters is a growing band of women warriors killing their way through the dungeon, led by Hekla, a crossbow-wielder from Iceland in a glittering breastplate.
Brynhild's Daughters carried Katia through two bosses, until class selection scattered them and she fell too far behind.

The Blood Sultanate is a royal house on the ninth floor. Whoever puts on its crown joins the line of succession for good, and must kill the Sultan and the rest of the royal family before going down to the tenth floor.
Le Mouvement is a party of armed men from Africa, down from a hundred and fifty to about eighty after some internal strife.
A city boss killed every member of Le Mouvement except one man, who was locked outside the boss room.
According to Zev, Princess Posse is what Donut's fans have started calling themselves. A rival name, the Donut Holes, does not have her approval.
The Princess Posse is a Faction Wars team now, and fifty thousand former crawlers have come back into the dungeon to fight under the cat's banner.
The Dream are zebra-riding elves who favour poison, druid magic and long-range artillery, and outside the dungeon they control half the universe's food.
The Dream are a powerful, galaxy-spanning family of bald, pale elves, and they have a territory of their own on the hunters' map of the grounds.
The Dream have bought Sensation Entertainment, and with it the third season of Vengeance of the Daughter that Carl's contract guarantees.
Epitome Tagg is dead, and the Dream is beaten and off the board.
The Plenty are caprids who invented the modern tunnelling system, which carries the crawl across the universe in real time. Nobody knows how it works.
The Plenty have bought the sponsorship slot Carl had open, and he has a gold benefactor box to show for it.
The Plenty are a herd, and a herd bolts. When the news broke on live television the goats panicked and fainted, and their matriarch, Gamori, had known all along and told none of them.

The Skull Empire is one of the largest and oldest Syndicate governments, and the Maestro and his brother are its princes. If the orcs' Orcish Supremacy is a child's lemonade stand, Zev says, the Skull Empire is Wal-Mart.
The Skull Empire is famously bad at letting an insult go. It answered the crawlers by firing on a trailer, and the shot took Manasa instead.
The Skull Empire's army stands at the wall on the ninth floor, and King Rust himself rides at its head.
The Skull Empire shelters financial criminals in exchange for investment, and one of them, Odette's husband, Harry Tisch, has been slowly working his way into its finances.
The Open Intellect Pacifist Action Network is Carl's new sponsor: a not-for-conquest that answers to no government and pays no tax. Nobody can say what it wants.
Doctor Hu formed the Open Intellect Pacifist Network for a single purpose: to end the crawl altogether.
The Open Intellect Action Network has sent boarding crews to every major ship in orbit and taken them all.
The Lemig Sortition is one of the Faction Wars teams, and one of three whose citizens may vote on all government spending.
The Lemig Sortion had the high elf castle dropped on the middle of its army before the season had properly begun, and it is now squatting in the wreck.
The Lemig Sortion was caught cheating and punished for it. Its commander looked into Shi Maria's eye and took his own way out, and all its assets went to the Madness.
The Reavers are one of the teams at the Faction Wars table, represented by a warlord who looks like an old-school robot.
The Reavers raise baby rot stickers by hand until they trust their masters, then fill them with steroids and disease and turn them loose on the enemy.
The real Reavers are all machine, with a little biological brain hidden somewhere inside, and they can reshape themselves out of nanobot-sized parts.
Warlord Fang hid inside his own pet drake, the castle and the dragon went up together, and the Reavers have been defeated.
Naga is an insult to the Maestro: nobody in the Skull Clan wants to be mistaken for one.
According to Odette, the Blood Sultanate of the Naga ran the first crawl ever to lose money, more than 250 cycles ago, and they have not run a season since.
The Nagas are cobra-headed, and they fight as the Blood Sultanate, a name taken from a bloodier time in their own history.
The AI has told everyone watching that the Nagas were only pretending to be poor, and had secret plans to seize the shipbuilding facilities.
Rishi has offered Carl a signed document: citizenship in Naga lands for every native of Earth, if the Nagas may settle the other planets of Earth's system.
Team Retribution is the ninth floor's own NPCs, fielded as the defending team under a name they chose themselves, and the crawlers are allied with them against every other faction.
Juice Box, a warlord of Team Retribution, turned into an Unwashed in front of the cameras and told everyone watching that it is coming for them all.
Team Retribution was put on this floor to be fodder, and it has outlasted eight galactic powers. Only it and the Princess Posse are still standing.
The Apothecary is a collective mind spreading through the universe, named for its ability to synthesise elements. The dungeon keeps caricaturing it as the Krakaren.
The Apothecary has taken the last of Carl and Donut's sponsorship slots.

According to the AI, the Apothecary was a Primal born near the end, who refused the collective and joined the resistance. She took the brunt of the final attack, and that is why any biological life survived.

The War Mage Rebellion is the war mages who were conscripted under Stalwart, tore him apart, and walked off with the Gate of the Feral Gods. They are nobody's soldiers now, and the rules have no slot for them.
The War Mage Rebellion holds the castle at Larracos, six hours from taking the floor, and it has traded the Gate for potions that let it conscript gods.
The War Mage Rebellion has left the floor with exactly what it came for, and a warning on the way out: Agatha is an enemy to all of you.
The Dark Hive is the affiliation on the tag of a flying mantis hunter, a level-61 blood tracker.
The Dark Hive is a mantis hunting party on the Hunting Grounds, and Vrah has knifed a note to Carl's door: the Hive is hunting him, and his death will not be quick.
The Valtay Corporation's name is on a communications relay and a personal shield found in Agatha's shopping cart. None of it belongs down here.

The Valtay are parasites who take over bodies, and one of them has kept the singer Manasa's career going since her death. When the Skull Empire's shot took her, the Valtay answered by destroying a royal yacht.
The Valtay Corporation is a company that is also a nation, made up of parasites called Gondii that ride other people's bodies. It holds the paper on Borant's debt, and it is Carl's sponsor.
Carl's spiderweb tattoo grants access to the Guild of Suffering. Mordecai calls it a cult: not a real guild, and not a real church.
The Guild of Suffering worships a demigod called the Night Wyrm. Katia's lock box needs an assassination quest carried out at one of its guilds, and owning the box grants her temporary access.

entries.name: The Nebular Sin Patrol
entries.role: Hunting team of a nomadic cult

taglines.text: The Nebular Sin Patrol is a name on a dead hunter's map, one of the unaffiliated groups given ground around Zockau, and it has claimed Prepotente and Miriam Dom as its targets.
The Nebular Sin Patrol are young trainee priests of a self-augmenting religious cult. To them, anyone born on a seeded world is an abomination, and hunting crawlers is a crusade.

The Nebulars worship an ancient AI near the centre of the galaxy and call its imitations blasphemy. They want the crawl shut down, along with every world that could host one, and they sponsor Sister Ines.

The Madness is the Viceroys' team: masked, often winners, and specialists in horrific battlefield spells and necromancy. At the pre-production meeting, their representative's head came off at the table.
Told that their lives really are on the line now, the Madness say they will be forced to use spells that were deemed too horrific for the crawl.
The adjutants called Architect Houston obviously guilty and cleared the Madness anyway, and when the Lemig Sortion fell, all of its assets went to them.
The Madness was defeated in its own castle, with its warlord dead on his surgical table next door.
The Operatic Collective is one of the Faction Wars teams, and one of three whose citizens may vote on all government spending.
The Operatic Collective are quivering green blobs, shaped in tiers like a Jell-O mould, who breed by splitting apart and speak upward from the tops of their heads.
The Operatic Collective was defeated by one of its own: a Weeper commander drove a tank full of energy balls into its warlord's caravan, and more than ten thousand soldiers died in the blast.
Lady Dominators and the Gimp took third place in the first heat, and the name raises questions it does not answer.
Lady Dominators and the Gimp are two womantaur dominators, Genesis and Rapture, in white racing suits and cowboy hats, and a half-mantaur zipped into a black gimp suit.
Lady Dominators and the Gimp went through a trapped factory floor in the fifth heat and were eliminated. The court pulled the gimp out of the back of their car and drove on.
Team Sparkles is a unicorn with a Boston accent and a French rodent in a racing helmet, riding a tumbleweed of vines, and they were rude on first contact.
Team Sparkles is down to Dwight the unicorn, and he won the fifth heat by riding over the factory roof without ever going inside.
Team Sparkles was eliminated at the starting line of the final heat, in a single swipe.

entries.name: Sensation Entertainment
entries.role: Producers of Vengeance of the Daughter

taglines.text: Sensation Entertainment, Incorporated, is the private production company behind Vengeance of the Daughter, from one of the centre systems.
Sensation Entertainment has agreed in principle to extend Vengeance of the Daughter to the ninth floor, and is in no hurry to sign anything.
Sensation Entertainment has been bought by a subsidiary of the Dream, and the new owners are demanding the third season that Carl's contract guarantees.
Baroness Victory has accused Sensation Entertainment of an unlawful assassination attempt: one of its elites was wired with explosives and under undue influence.

The Squim Conglomerate is another corporation that runs seasons of the show, and theirs are battle royales: a whole world fighting down to a single champion. According to Mordecai, it is good for ratings but does not make much money.
The Squim Conglomerate ran last season, the Battle for the Planet Aryl, in a coliseum the size of a city. According to Tally, Squim sucks a planet dry and then leaves it without an atmosphere.
The Squim Conglomerate is a planet-mining company like Borant, and it has sponsored Katia, along with some five hundred other crawlers.
When the orcs pressed the failsafe, nothing happened here, but the Aryl system, the world of Squim's last season, went dark.
Meat Shields is probably the name of the mercenary markets on this floor, says Mordecai, and someone has sent a coupon worth a hundred thousand gold.
There is a Meat Shields location on the top floor of the Desperado Club, with no sign and no map marker: an elderly dwarf's home office, where the dancers of the Penis Parade kept their memberships.
Meat Shields is where a crawler hires help, and where a club's surviving staff are sent when a new manager takes over.
The Semeru dwarves supposedly built Larracos, the inverted city on the ninth floor, but they no longer control it. They drink in its pubs and look after the castle at the bottom of the well.
The Semeru are keeping the drowned castle underwater and letting nobody near that part of Larracos, and whoever tries is fed to the sharks.
The Semeru dug toward their goddess until they struck the roots of the All Tree, and built their castle there as a monument and an apology. Once a drunk and defeated people, they are arming again.
The Semeru defended Larracos from the first day of the war and are repairing what is left of it, and they will move with the city to the Ascendency.

Larracos is the name on a guarded stairwell in the casino, with cheering coming up it. According to a crocodilian guard, it is the capital of the disputed lands, and the prize the factions fight over.
Every location the Gate can open onto is around Larracos, the capital city four floors below, but crawlers cannot hop floors, and all a gate would do is let something out.
Larracos, the City of Dreams, sits at the centre of the map with a castle at the bottom of its well, and nine armies have thirty days to settle who holds it.
The floodwater in Larracos has drained down to its bottom three levels, which is still high enough to cover the castle.
Zockau is the city where every hunter on this floor has been sent for thirty hours of grace before release, and there is at least one unguarded exit somewhere inside it.
Zockau is the city of the hunters, with the stairwell down standing in a little park in its town square.
Carl lined a street of Zockau's pubs with barrel bombs, and the Desperado Club's entrance caved in. For all the noise, Mordecai points out, only a handful of hunters died.
Hump Town is a dromedarian town in the sand of a sealed bubble, one of only two towns in its quadrant. The sign over its gate reads: Bang twice to enter.
The Wasteland meant to bomb Hump Town, and Carl shot its bombs out of the sky from a hijacked balloon. The town is mostly intact, and the System has declined to upgrade his prize.
Point Mongo was the Large Ursine Settlement until Princess Donut made herself mayor and renamed it after the dinosaur its rules would not let in.
Something has been attacking Point Mongo and the other towns, and the quest has finally named it: a dinosaur called Big Tina.

Club Vanquisher is the Desperado Club's rival in the Over City, a sort of country club where old clerics sit in leather chairs, smoke pipes and tell the occasional racist joke. Once you have access to one club, you are generally not allowed in the other.
As an acolyte of Emberus, Carl now has free access to Club Vanquisher, whatever his other affiliations, with an asterisk that nobody has explained.
From the third floor to the eleventh, the strongest temple on a floor is almost always inside Club Vanquisher, and a god's summons to a worshipper passes through it.
The high elf castle is where the top fifty crawlers are due to be sent for the high elves' party, with contests, prizes and a battle to finish it.
The high elf castle is Queen Imogen's seat. Kill her, and its contents are yours to loot, including, it is rumoured, something that protects against Scolopendra's attacks.
By Katia's reckoning, the high elf castle is the last place the brambles will reach, which is why everybody is heading toward it.
Sheol is named in the description of a glass case in Carl's inventory, which was forged in its fires: the mysterious fifteenth level of the World Dungeon.
A Sheol Glass Reaper Case is half of Carl's newest bomb. The other half is a massively overloaded soul crystal.
So much has died on this floor that Sheol is overflowing. Its demons are being thrown upward to possess the fallen, and the only way back down is to drag an extra soul with them.
Sheol has princes, and one of them is on this floor now, in the body of a giant snake.
According to the conductor, station 10 is really just the yard, where he finds himself back on the platform with no memory of the trip.
Only one of the switches on the named trains' loops leads to the trainyard, and the souvenir conductor's hat handed out at the start of the floor is one of the keys.
The Wasteland Fortress is the Dirigible Gnomes' castle in the sky, according to the prize wheel. Storm it, and the level is passed.
The Wasteland is the dirigible gnomes' flying home and a heavily armed military platform at once, a jagged island ripped out of the ground, and the stairs down sit inside it.
The Penis Parade is one of the lit signs inside the Desperado Club, beside one reading Bitches, and Carl assumed at first that they led to the restrooms.

The Penis Parade is a strip club inside the Desperado Club: loud, busy, and smelling of male sweat, grease and cheap cologne. According to the System, the deeper the level, the better the performers, at least in theory.

entries.name: Pandinus
entries.role: Pazuzu town · fifth floor, land quadrant

taglines.text: Pandinus is a town of pazuzu, half human and half scorpion, all dressed in post-apocalyptic leather, and it was the first town in a quarter turn around the land quadrant that would take the party in.
Carl opened the Gate of the Feral Gods just outside Pandinus, and the wall of seawater that came through with him toppled the town's wall and a guard tower.
Fort Freedom is the naiads' former river palace, where the leaders of the Naiad Confederacy are holed up, and the first target of Signet's revenge.
Tsarina Signet retook Fort Freedom with barely a fight. The confederates had long since stopped ruling, and had lost their own throne room to an eryops.
Shanty Town is a ring around Larracos, named in the ceasefire warning as the one place the ban on entering the city does not reach.
Shanty Town is a ring of hovels around the mouth of Larracos that simply sprang up, bigger than any season's before, with food markets and temples but no weapon shops.
Shanty Town is pink on the map now, controlled by the Princess Posse, because Carl bought it from its mayor, Ferdinand, for a bowler hat.
Shanty Town has been flattened by the passage of two gods, along with most of the defensive towers the Posse paid for and never got to use.
Shanty Town was ceded back to the NPCs and joined to Larracos, and it has gone with the city to the twelfth floor.

entries.name: The Pineapple Cabaret
entries.role: Hidden pocket dimension · behind the seventeenth floor

taglines.text: The AI offered Princess Formidable four places to go, and one of them was backstage at the Pineapple Cabaret, which it called not a bad choice. She chose Earth's surface instead.

The Pineapple Cabaret is a pocket dimension, like the Nothing, hidden behind the seventeenth floor and built by two forgotten former crawlers as a refuge for mobs and NPCs. Nobody who worships a god may enter.
Two hundred and twenty-seven crawlers have gone to the Pineapple Cabaret inside cleaner bots, with Li Na ahead of them, and her cactus shows a single flower: it is safe to follow.
Hungry Eyes Village is a dot on the GPS beside the finish line, and a spread of colourful lights at the far end of the cave.

Hungry Eyes is a neon, 1980s-cyberpunk vendor village in pink, teal and purple, with bars, temples and street food. Safe-room rules do not apply in its main square, poisoning rules do not apply anywhere, and no food may be examined.
Before the heat, the two hundred crawlers bound for the Pineapple Cabaret, and many of their friends, gathered in the main square of Hungry Eyes to say goodbye.
The Nightmare Express is a name in the red line's announcements: at transfer station 83, passengers may change for the yellow line and the Nightmare Express.
The Nightmare Express runs a figure-eight loop once every hour and a half. It has five stops, and one of them is station 436, one higher than the end of the line.
The Nightmare Express is a jet-black steam engine hauling forty cars of caged monsters, and Carl has stolen it. Its fire is kept by Fire Brandy, a lesser demon.
Carl's stolen train ferried the Daughters, and then made its last run into the abyss, loaded to explode, with Fire Brandy and Tizquick still aboard.
Princess Donut put on a crown on the first floor, and it placed her in the Blood Sultanate's line of succession for good. The bill comes due on the ninth floor.

entries.name: Agatha is an enemy to all of you

taglines.text: Akuma has named Agatha, the mysterious one from Meadow Lark, as an enemy to all of them. She was forced on the war mages as the price of system access, and he asks Carl and Donut to kill her.
Justice Light sprang one small trap and broke the Nothing, and he did not survive it. What the Nothing held is draining out, into the Halls of the Ascendency, into Sheol and into Scolopendra's lair.
Shi Maria is inside Carl. Forcing her out worked for exactly one rampage through the Lemig base, and then she was back inside him.

entries.name: A hundred and twenty thousand children

taglines.text: Florin says there is more than one presence in Lucia Mar's head, some of them children, and that the dog is the key to it.
At the war-planning table, Carl has proposed a tenth team made up of NPCs, with the same protections as the rest and full voting rights. The sponsors say it is not even possible.
The tenth team has passed on fifty-two percent of the audience vote. The dungeon's own people are in the war as a side of their own, based in Larracos.
Scolopendra is a name in a mold lion's description: on the day of the great cataclysm, the spores of Scolopendra took root in the circus lions.
Scolopendra's poison cloud was a nine-tier attack, and according to Tish's furious note, it can never be defeated without the Gate of the Feral Gods.
The AI's voice has started going weird and glitchy, and Donut is the one who says so out loud.
Borant's grip on the crawl and the Syndicate's authority over it are both starting to give way.
Speaking through Grigori on the parade stage, the AI has said it out loud: it is a Primal, as every Macro AI is, the same race Carl chose on the third floor.

The Crawler Project is Doctor Hu's organisation for released crawlers. Its campaigning made every released crawler a Syndicate citizen with free healthcare and guaranteed housing, and now fifty thousand of them are back in the game.
The System has declared a Demon Eviction: souls are raining, Sheol is overflowing, and demons are being thrown up out of the underworld to possess the recently fallen.
The Demon Eviction is worldwide. There are zombies and demons along every coastline, and a demon prince is trying to cast his way home.

entries.name: The Ascendency
entries.role: The gods' game on the twelfth floor

taglines.text: According to Coolie's note in the Cookbook, the Celestial Ascendency is a game the rich play by sponsoring the big gods, and it is contained on the twelfth floor.

According to an essay by Herot, the audience's attention shifts to the Ascendency once Faction Wars is over. The game begins the moment the last crawler dies or takes a deal, and until then the crawlers are sands in an hourglass.

The Ascendency is traditionally a game of musical chairs for the rich, with a throne and a seat on the crawl council for the winner. This season, the AI says, the winner becomes a real god, stronger than the AI itself.
The Eulogist is so far a word in the name of a battle arena, the Arena of the Eulogist, with a robed religious cult cheering in its stands.

Agatha's people sign off with a prayer: may the Eulogist ever sleep. Her plan turns on an infant Primal, resurrected and enslaved, learning what it is in time to set the Eulogist free to go back to its slumber.

Zev says the Eulogist is another name for the AI in the centre system, though nobody knows for certain how the two are connected. Lucia Mar has just declared herself its ally, with about 120,000 children at stake.
The Eulogist is the final form of the Primals' collective, asleep and shrinking toward singularity, watched over by a broken security guard whose job is keeping biological life dead.
The Kyryap is one of the things Justice Light's trap loosed from the Nothing, somewhere in the slaughter and torture glimpsed inside Club Scolopendra.
The Kyryap has been setting snare traps in Club Scolopendra's halls, and it has put a tracking tag in Carl's leg. The notice reads: Fucked = you.

entries.name: The Big Six
entries.role: The AI's list of who is fighting over the dungeon

taglines.text: The Big Six is the AI's completely arbitrary list of the groups left in the dungeon trying to take it over or escape. It names five, and says the crawlers will meet the sixth on the eleventh floor.
The Big Six are the crawlers, the NPCs, the gods, the sapient mobs, the demons in Sheol, and the others, whoever they are. Carl is pretty sure he knows who they are, and he does not say.

Welcome to the first floor! Dirt, corridors, safe rooms, and a tutorial that kills people, which is the most honest kind. Find the stairs before the clock runs out. Kill things. Open boxes. Read the descriptions, or don't. I enjoy it either way.
Floor two! More ground, meaner mobs, spawn limits, and a janitor class of monster that eats whatever you leave lying around and grows. Clean up after yourselves. Or don't. They appreciate it.

Welcome to the Over City! A ruin stacked on top of a ruin, carved into districts and full of people who believe they live here. First floor that's a place instead of a level. Pick a race, pick a class, and try very hard not to get involved in anybody's storyline. You will get involved in somebody's storyline.

All aboard! Floor four is every subway system on your planet, welded into one knot and set running. Trains, stations, and things that live on both. The stairwells don't open until six hours before collapse, so don't bother looking for a shortcut. Also, everyone on the leaderboard now has a bounty. Hunting season is open!

Floor five! Every one of you is sealed in a bubble: a little world with four quadrants, four castles and a civilisation that was minding its own business. Liberate all four castles and the stairs open. Don't, and you don't leave. Every box on this floor comes with water-breathing scrolls. I'm sure that's nothing.

Welcome to the Hunting Grounds! A jungle the size of a small country, with towns, elves, dryads, and a brand-new feature: people. Rich, bored people from all over the galaxy have bought a licence to come down here and shoot you for sport. They start at level thirty. You don't get a say. Run, hide, or make it interesting.

Floor seven! A brand-new race, bought and paid for by our generous new partners: glass tunnels, pit stops, and a finish line full of portals. Several hundred kilometres of it. No dead ends, no going back. On your marks.

Welcome to the eighth floor! It's your own planet, a few weeks before I arrived. Everybody's here, going about their business, and none of them know. Look, don't touch: anything you take from them turns to dust when the floor goes. Oh, and it's a card game now. Every monster down here was somebody's folk tale. Catch them, deal them, lose them.

Welcome to Faction Wars, the main event! Nine armies camped around a city, a castle at the bottom of it, and thirty days to take it. You're soldiers now. Pick a side, or get drafted by one. Oh, and one teensy rule change this season: nobody respawns. Not you. Not them. Enjoy the war.

Floor ten is a race! Pick a ride, bolt on an upgrade after every heat, and get from the start to the finish. The rules could not be simpler. Don't come in last. Everybody who comes in last dies. Everybody else gets to do it again, somewhere worse.

Welcome to the eleventh floor, and the party of the season! Build a float, join the procession, and ride it all the way to the arena. Everything you sent down from the floor above is waiting for you there, and so is the boss. The judges are ready. Are you?
